children: Goldman Sachs strategist Tony Pasquariello has a blunt message for AI stock investors: stop demanding precise returns from spending companies consider unavoidable.
Hyperscaler capital expenditures are expected to surge from $154 billion in 2023 to more than $1.3 trillion by 2028. That spending includes commitments from Meta Platforms

Pasquariello argues that judging those investments through ROIC is overly simplistic. AI can create value by improving operations, but it also represents defensive spending needed to prevent competitors from disrupting existing businesses.
What Goldman's AI View Means for Investors

The strategist compared the current cycle with early cloud adoption and cybersecurity spending. Companies could not always calculate an immediate return from those investments, yet refusing to spend risked leaving their businesses less competitive or exposed.

Calculating precise AI returns is difficult because adoption remains early. Goldman partner George Lee also believes competition could transfer the technology's financial value to consumers through better products and lower prices instead of expanding corporate profits.

That possibility does not eliminate the incentive to invest. Weak or uncertain direct returns may coexist with continued capital spending because companies cannot afford to surrender technological ground.

Pasquariello remains structurally bullish on the long-term AI investment trend, but he expects a less orderly climb. Political scrutiny ahead of the midterms, concerns surrounding safety and malicious uses, and electricity-grid bottlenecks could create market dislocations similar to the DeepSeek shock.

For investors, the distinction is crucial. Rising AI spending can support infrastructure demand without guaranteeing equal returns across every stock. Investors should monitor adoption, productivity improvements, free cash flow and power availability rather than expecting a definitive ROIC figure. AI-focused funds including the Global X Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF (AIQ) and Amplify AI Powered Equity ETF (AIEQ) offer exposure, but remain vulnerable to volatility across the theme.

title: Goldman Sachs Has Blunt Message for AI Stock Investors
